messages.subject: htmlOutput & Link To Windows File
parts:
This is a general R/Windows/Shiny question.

My Problem:

I would like to create a link in the UI sidebar to a file hosted on another Windows computer on the same network that the users run the Shiny app from. The link should open an html file from the networked computer in the browser.

I am doing this by using renderText in the server file to paste a string of html code together containing the file path and then calling htmlOutput in the ui file.

My issue is that the address returned by my link does not point to the file. I need some input on how to paste a text string together that points to a Windows network file using html.

server.R

output$link_text = renderText({
        lnk1 <- paste("<p> <font face='Helvetica' size='1'> <b> Raw MS Data: </b> <br> <a href=",'"',sep="")
        lnk2 <- paste("\\\\networkpc\\f\\folder\\input$batch\\index.html",sep="")
        lnk3 <- paste('"',">",sep="")
        lnk4 <- paste("//networkpc/f/folder/input$batch]/index.html","</a>.</font></p>",sep="")

        link = paste(lnk1,lnk2,lnk3,lnk4,sep="")
        return(link)
    })

ui.R
htmlOutput("link_text")

When I click on the resulting link I get the following path in my browser. This does not open the file successfully in the browser and the file can't be found.
http://networkpc/f/folder/OM0010617-MSP/index.html

When I manually navigate to the target file in Windows...it successfully opens in my browser and the file path displayed in the browser is:
file://networkpc/f/folder/OM0010617-MSP/index.html

Question:
How do I replace the "http:" in the link with "file:"?

messages.subject: Re: htmlOutput & Link To Windows File
parts:
So I seem to have resolved the link format issue by adding "file:" to the link address text.

So now the issue is that when I click on the link in shiny....nothing happens.

When I right-click and copy the link address...then paste it into my browser...it opens the target html file successfully.

Is there a particular reason shiny wouldn't allow the opening of networked files when the users pc ison the same intranet/network as the file?
